structured_output.summary: Two defects in code that is already written, plus two release-pipeline gaps that fail closed. The guardian and R example code read as largely sound on a read-through. I ran no code. The only command I ran was a read-only `git ls-tree` in a subdirectory, to confirm the monorepo finding. I could not compare against SPEC revision 7 line by line.

findings.title: Site audit returns an empty route set for a package in a repo subdirectory
findings.body: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <sha>` runs with cwd=root. In a subdirectory it returns only that subtree, with paths relative to cwd. I confirmed this in `lib/`. The code keeps only paths with `p.startswith(prefix)` and then strips `prefix`. For a nested package where `prefix` is e.g. `pkg/`, every path is dropped. `expected` is empty, `_pkgdown.yml` is never found, and `config['url']` is never checked. All sitemap article and reference routes are then reported as `site-extra-page`, and the stage still ends `complete`. The `head_paths` check `prefix + file not in head_paths` mixes relative and full paths, so every working-tree page is labelled 'dirty-tree'. `select_ref` also reads `.github/workflows` from `root`, not the repo top level, so a nested package misses its deployment workflow and silently falls back to `main`.
findings.recommendation: Use `ls-tree --full-tree`, or `--full-name` with consistent prefix stripping. Resolve workflows from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Add a nested-package fixture test.

findings.title: Nothing produces the independent R/HTTP fixture evidence the verifier requires
findings.body: The runner needs `fixture-executions.json`, and the verifier needs `R`, `R_packages`, `reported_r_checked` and `reported_http_checked`. A repo-wide grep found no code that writes any of them, so no run can pass `validate_run`. This fails closed, so it is a missing implementation and not a false pass. The CI workflow also never runs `verify_a2_release.py main` or `validate_aggregate` across the two platform artifacts. The requirement ledger, spec hash, runtime lock and cross-platform checks are therefore never run in CI. Once something writes `fixture-executions.json`, it will be a file in the same output directory the pytest run can write to. Pytest-side code could then forge the 'independent' oracle. `evidence.update(...)` would also let that file overwrite `candidate_sha` and the hashes.
findings.recommendation: Collect the R version and package versions in the runner with its own Rscript call. Write oracle evidence from a separate process with an allowlisted schema. Add a final CI job that downloads both artifacts and runs the verifier.

findings.title: Guardian output cap is poll-based and the process-group check can race with pgid reuse
findings.body: The 10 MiB cap is checked by `stat` every 50 ms, so a fast writer can emit far more before SIGTERM, and nothing caps the file size. After `process.poll()` reaps the leader, `killpg(pid, 0)` and the later SIGTERM/SIGKILL use a pgid that can be recycled once the group is empty, so a late `killpg` could hit an unrelated group. The window is small. During startup the guardian never reads `heartbeat.json`, so a parent slower than 5 s to arm is declared 'parent-loss' while still alive. This is inferred from the code.
findings.recommendation: Apply `RLIMIT_FSIZE` to the child. Only call `killpg` while the leader is unreaped, or track group members. Read heartbeats in the startup loop too.

findings.title: Partial results counted after a deadline kill; raw child output embedded in the report
findings.body: After a `deadline` or `output-limit` termination, records already written to `result.json` still increment `counts['checked']`, although the stage is marked incomplete. Up to 1 MiB each of R stdout and stderr is copied into `stage['provenance']`. R inherits the full environment, so tokens that README code prints could leak into the report. Any option beyond the supported literals, such as `fig.width`, raises and blocks the whole README as incomplete. That is conservative and may over-block real packages.
findings.recommendation: Count a segment as checked only when the lifecycle completed. Truncate or redact diagnostic output. Consider ignoring harmless options such as `fig.*`.

next_steps: Fix the ls-tree prefix handling in `_docsite.audit` and add a nested-package test.
Implement independent fixture-execution and R-version/package evidence collection, and add a CI aggregate verification job.
Harden guardian output limiting and pgid handling.
